title: Ext vanishing over a regular local ring
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] and $d=\dim R$ its Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Then $\operatorname{Ext}^q_R(M,N)=0$ [def-pc-ext] for every finitely generated $R$-module $M$, every $R$-module $N$ and every integer $q>d$.

source.place: Lemma lemma-Ext-0-regular (Tag 0FZ3), proof of (1), invoking Algebra Proposition Tag 00O7

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-finite-gl-dim] (Stacks Tag 00O7), every $R$-module, in particular $M$, has a projective resolution of length $\le d$. Here $d$ is finite because a regular local ring is Noetherian and its maximal ideal has a finite set of generators; the cited theorem states the bound with this $d$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-projective-dimension-ext-characterization] (Stacks Tag 065R) with $X=M$ and $n=d$. Step 1 supplies its projective-resolution hypothesis, so $\operatorname{Ext}^i_R(M,N)=0$ for every $R$-module $N$ and every $i\ge d+1$. Since the integer $q>d$ is equivalent to $q\ge d+1$, taking $i=q$ proves the claim. In particular $q$ is nonnegative, as required by [def-pc-ext].
